samples.reference:
# Community Gardening Project Plan

## Introduction
The community gardening project aims to create a green space where residents can engage in gardening activities, grow their own produce, and foster a sense of community. This plan outlines the various aspects of the project, from site selection to maintenance, ensuring a well-structured and successful initiative.

## Objectives
- To provide a communal space for gardening and relaxation.
- To promote sustainable living and environmental awareness.
- To enhance community engagement and social interaction.
- To produce fresh, organic vegetables and fruits for community members.
- To educate participants on gardening techniques and plant care.

## Site Selection
The ideal site for the community garden should be easily accessible to all residents, receive ample sunlight, and have good drainage. Potential locations include unused public land, school grounds, or community centers. A site visit will be conducted to assess soil quality, water availability, and existing vegetation. The final selection will be made based on community feedback and practical considerations.

## Design and Layout
The garden will be designed to maximize space and functionality. It will include raised beds for easy access, pathways for wheelchair users, and designated areas for different types of plants. A central gathering area with benches will be provided for socializing and educational events. The layout will be documented in a detailed map and shared with all participants.

## Plant Selection
A variety of plants will be chosen to cater to different tastes and growing conditions. Vegetables such as tomatoes, lettuce, and carrots will be prioritized due to their popularity and ease of cultivation. Herbs and flowers will also be included to attract pollinators and enhance the aesthetic appeal of the garden. A plant list will be compiled and distributed to participants for reference.

## Maintenance Schedule
A regular maintenance schedule will be established to ensure the garden remains healthy and productive. Tasks will include watering, weeding, pruning, and pest control. A rotating schedule will be created to assign responsibilities to volunteers, ensuring that no one is overburdened. Monthly meetings will be held to review progress and address any issues.

## Community Involvement
Community involvement is crucial for the success of the project. Volunteers will be recruited through local advertisements, social media, and community events. Training sessions will be organized to teach participants about gardening basics and specific plant care. Regular events such as potlucks and workshops will be held to build camaraderie and encourage ongoing participation.

## Budget
A budget will be created to cover the costs of materials, tools, and any necessary permits. Funding will be sought through grants, sponsorships, and community donations. A detailed budget plan will be developed and reviewed periodically to ensure financial sustainability.

## Timeline
The project will be organized into phases to ensure a smooth implementation:
- **Month 1:** Site selection and community engagement
- **Month 2:** Design and layout planning
- **Month 3:** Preparation of the site and procurement of materials
- **Month 4:** Installation of raised beds and planting
- **Month 5-6:** Ongoing maintenance and community events
- **Month 7:** Evaluation and planning for the next season

This timeline will be flexible to accommodate any unforeseen challenges and ensure the project meets its goals.

samples.input:
在监督学习中，过拟合与欠拟合是影响模型泛化性能的核心问题。欠拟合通常源于模型容量不足或特征表达能力有限，导致训练误差和测试误差同时偏高，体现为高偏差；过拟合则发生在模型过于复杂、对训练数据中的噪声和偶然模式进行学习时，训练误差很低但测试误差显著升高，表现为高方差。这两者本质上体现了偏差—方差权衡。

针对欠拟合问题，常见方法包括提升模型复杂度、引入更具判别力的特征、采用非线性模型或集成学习等；而缓解过拟合则需要控制模型自由度，例如通过正则化（L1/L2 正则）、参数约束、特征选择、数据增强以及降低模型容量。交叉验证可用于稳定评估模型泛化误差，避免因数据划分带来的评估偏差。

在训练过程中，学习曲线是诊断过拟合与欠拟合的重要工具。若训练与验证误差均较高，通常指向欠拟合；若二者差距较大，则暗示过拟合。此外，早停（Early Stopping）通过监控验证集损失，在性能恶化前终止训练，是深度学习中常用的隐式正则化手段。

总体而言，过拟合与欠拟合并非孤立问题，而是与数据规模、噪声水平、模型复杂度及优化策略密切相关。通过在模型能力与数据约束之间取得平衡，结合系统性的验证与正则化手段，才能获得具有良好泛化能力的学习模型。

 the dilute bose - condensed gases , the spatial coherence can be investigated directly by interfering two bose condensates . for two coherently separated becs , because the relative phase of two sub - condensates is locked , 
 it is not surprising that there is a clear interference pattern when the two sub - condensates are allowed to overlap . in the celebrated experiment by andrews _ 
 et al _ @xcite , however , high - contrast fringes were observed even for two completely independent condensates at an initial time . in this experiment , to prepare two initially independent condensates , the dilute bose gases were evaporatively cooled in a double - well potential created by splitting a magnetic trap in half with a far - off blue - detuned laser beam ( see also @xcite ) . 
 in particular , the height of the external potential due to the laser beam is much larger than the chemical potential of two separated condensates , which means that the tunneling current can be safely omitted . after switching off the double - well potential , the two initially independent condensates overlapped and high - contrast fringes 
 were observed in ref . 
 this experimental result shows clearly that there is a spatial coherence property after the overlapping between two independent interacting condensates . 
 although high - contrast fringes were observed for two initially independent condensates , in many literature ( see for example leggett , pethick , stringari and references therein ) , it is shown that there is no interference term in the dens...

after removing the double - well potential trapping two initially independent bose condensates , the density expectation value is calculated when both the exchange symmetry of identical bosons and interatomic interaction are considered . 
 the density expectation value and evolution equations are obtained based on both the first - quantization and second - quantization methods . 
 when the interatomic interaction is considered carefully , after the overlapping of two initially independent condensates , it is shown that there is a nonzero interference term in the density expectation value . 
 it is found that the calculated density expectation value with this model agrees with the interference pattern observed in the experiment by andrews _ 
 et al _ _ 
 ( science * 275 * , 637 ( 1997))_. the nonzero interference term in the density expectation value physically arises from the exchange symmetry of identical bosons and interatomic interaction which make two initially independent condensates become coherent after the overlapping . for two initially independent condensates , our researches show that there is an interaction - induced coherence process .

interstellar gas in the solar neighborhood has a variety of thermal and chemical phases , including cold atomic gas inside or mixed with cold molecular clouds ( e.g. , sato & fukui 1978 ) , cool and warm atomic gas on the envelopes of molecular clouds ( chromey et al . 
 1989 ; andersson & wannier 1993 ; wannier et al . 
 1993 ) and in the diffuse , low density medium ( kulkarni & heiles 1987 ) , cold molecules in dark and dense clouds ( combes 1991 ) and in translucent clouds ( magnani , blitz & mundy 1985 ) , warm molecules in dense clouds near embedded luminous stars ( e.g. , cesaroni et al . 1994 ) , dense photo - ionized gas in the neighborhoods of o and b - type stars , low - density ionized gas between these stars ( walterbos & braun 1994 ; reynolds 1995 ; ferguson et al . 1996 ) , and hot , shock - heated gas near supernovae and windy stars ( ostriker & mckee 1988 ) . 
 there is also considerable variety in the types of molecules that are present inside dark clouds , ranging from primarily h@xmath0 in translucent clouds ( spitzer & jenkins 1975 ; magnani et al . 
 1998 ) , with a possible trace of pah or long - chain molecules ( leger & puget 1984 ; tulej et al . 1998 ) , to a mixture of complex molecules in dense clouds ( e.g. , langer et al . 1997 
 ; see reviews by van dishoeck and thaddeus , this conference ) . 
 the thermal and chemical states of the cold and cool gas have such a great variety because the clouds shield themselves to different levels from photodissociative radiation and radiant heating . 
 this makes the molecular abundance and temperature depend on density , column density , metallicity , age , and local radiation field , all of which vary from cloud to cloud and with radius in the galaxy . 
 the nature of cloud _ structure _ does not change this much , because it is largely the result of turbulence , self - gravity , and local explosions , which seem to act the same way everywhere .
